summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: True coelom (eucoelom) is completely enclosed by mesoderm. Aschelminthes have a pseudocoel (mesodermal pouches in blastocoel), and Platyhelminthes have solid mesodermal parenchyma (acoelomate).

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 1. Germ Layer Configuration
• **Diploblastic**: Animals derived from two embryonic primary germ layers: outer **ectoderm** and inner **endoderm**, separated by an undifferentiated non-cellular gelatinous matrix called **mesoglea** (e.g., *Porifera*, *Cnidaria*, *Ctenophora*).
• **Triploblastic**: Animals derived from three embryonic germ layers: outer **ectoderm**, middle **mesoderm**, and inner **endoderm** (e.g., *Platyhelminthes* through *Chordata*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Coelom (Body Cavity) Architecture & Origin
conceptBreakdown.title: Coelom (Body Cavity) Architecture & Origin
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
COELOM ARCHITECTURES

ACOELOMATE                PSEUDOCOELOMATE             EUCOELOMATE (True Coelom)
(No Cavity)               (False Cavity)              (Fully Mesodermal Lined)

┌───────────────┐         ┌───────────────┐           ┌───────────────┐
│ Ectoderm      │         │ Ectoderm      │           │ Ectoderm      │
├───────────────┤         ├───────────────┤           ├───────────────┤
│ Solid         │         │ Mesodermal    │           │ Somatopleure  │
│ Parenchyma    │         │ Pouches       │           ├───────────────┤
│ Mesoderm      │         ├───────────────┤           │ COELOMIC CAVITY│
├───────────────┤         │ Persistent    │           ├───────────────┤
│ Endoderm      │         │ Blastocoel    │           │ Splanchnopleure│
└───────────────┘         ├───────────────┤           ├───────────────┤
                          │ Endoderm      │           │ Endoderm      │
                          └───────────────┘           └───────────────┘
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Acoelomate**: Body cavity is completely absent; the space between gut and outer body wall is filled with solid mesodermal parenchyma tissue (e.g., *Platyhelminthes*).
• **Pseudocoelomate**: Body cavity is **not** lined continuously by mesoderm. Instead, mesoderm exists as scattered pouches within a persistent embryonic blastocoel (e.g., *Aschelminthes* / *Nematoda*).
• **Eucoelomate (True Coelomate)**: Body cavity lined on both sides by mesoderm (outer parietal / somatopleuric mesoderm and inner visceral / splanchnopleuric mesoderm).
  - **Schizocoelomate**: True coelom formed by the **splitting of solid mesodermal blocks** (e.g., *Annelida*, *Arthropoda*, *Mollusca*).
  - **Enterocoelomate**: True coelom formed by **outpocketings of the embryonic archenteron** (primitive gut) (e.g., *Echinodermata*, *Hemichordata*, *Chordata*).

conceptBreakdown.title: 1.3 Protostome vs. Deuterostome Developmental Profiles
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
BILATERIAN DEVELOPMENTAL LINES
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
   PROTOSTOMIA                                             DEUTEROSTOMIA
 (Mouth First)                                           (Anus First)
  ├── Spiral & Determinate Cleavage                       ├── Radial & Indeterminate Cleavage
  ├── Blastopore becomes MOUTH                            ├── Blastopore becomes ANUS
  └── Schizocoelous Origin                                └── Enterocoelous Origin
      (Annelids, Arthropods, Molluscs)                        (Echinoderms, Hemichordates, Chordates)
conceptBreakdown.content:
| Trait | Protostome Lineage | Deuterostome Lineage |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cleavage Pattern** | **Spiral** (spindle axes oblique to egg axis) and **Determinate / Mosaic** (cell fate fixed at cleavage) | **Radial** (spindle axes parallel/perpendicular) and **Indeterminate / Regulative** (totipotent early blastomeres) |
| **Fate of Blastopore** | Blastopore develops into the **Mouth**; anus forms secondary opening | Blastopore develops into the **Anus**; mouth forms secondary opening |
| **Coelom Formation** | **Schizocoely** (splitting of mesodermal masses) | **Enterocoely** (archenteric pouching) |
| **Phylogenetic Phyla** | *Annelida*, *Arthropoda*, *Mollusca* | *Echinodermata*, *Hemichordata*, *Chordata* |
